newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Attorney General delays Mass. Electric deal.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Attorney General delays Mass. Electric deal.

text.p: The Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities said it has determined that a settlement proposed by Massachusetts Electric Co to restructure its assets is consistent with its "goals and principles."
However, the DPU said in a letter two areas of the settlement are inconsistent with its principles and precedents, and therefore would have to defer final judgement on its decision.
"We commit to respond with final action no more than thirty days after receipt of amendments to the settlement that address the department's concerns," the DPU Chairman John Howe wrote.

New England Electric System affiliate Massachusetts Electric Co proposed the settlement in September to sell or spin off ownership of its power plants to non-affiliated companies in exchange for the ability to recover sunk costs during the transition to a competitive electricity market.

Under the plan, sunk costs would be recovered through a transitional access charge on retail distribution rates, Mass. Electric said. In addition, the utility would give consumers a 10 percent cut in rates near-term.

"Essentially, it's been endorsed or approved," Mass. Electric spokeswoman Susan Stevens told Reuters. "We're very happy with that. There are two minor issues that we're very confident we can resolve very quickly."
Howe said two technical points on bundling costs were inconsistent with the DPU's principles and, as well, financing provisons of the settlement are premarture.
